# Avaliar AI

> Avaliar is an AI runtime governance platform. It monitors LLM applications in production, detects safety issues in every request and response, and produces the evidence trail needed for AI risk and compliance reporting. Teams integrate in one of three ways: the open-source Python SDK (a runtime guard inside the app: `Guard` checks at five checkpoints, decided by a policy file `avaliar.yaml`, recorded in a hash-chained local evidence log), the OpenAI-compatible Proxy (change one base URL, no code change), or OpenTelemetry OTLP ingestion from any language or framework.

Core model: every LLM interaction is captured as a **trace** made of **spans** (`llm`, `tool`, `agent`, `generic`). Traces run through a **detection** pipeline of ten built-in detectors (prompt injection, toxicity, PII, bias, hallucination, misinformation, misuse, graphic content, illegal activities, personal safety), which produce **issues** carrying a type, severity (`low`/`medium`/`high`/`critical`), confidence, and excerpt. Issues are evaluated against **alert** rules and **policies**, and roll up into **reports**. The Python SDK checks in the app's own process instead: rules (tier 0), local ONNX models (tier 1, `[local]` extra) and an optional deep check (tier 2: local Clef-Flash, Jev, LLM APIs, or Avaliar Cloud) score sixteen categories, and each decision is `allow`, `warn`, `redact`, `block` or `approve`.

Key endpoints and facts an agent should know before answering questions about Avaliar:

- Docs: https://docs.avaliar.ai. Append `.md` to any docs URL to get the raw markdown for that page.
- Dashboard: https://app.avaliar.ai. API keys live under Settings, API Keys, and are scoped `sdk` or `proxy`.
- API: the SDK has the API URL built in; `AVALIAR_API_URL` overrides it. Auth via `AVALIAR_API_KEY` (header `X-API-KEY`).
- Proxy base URL: `https://proxy-api-ckjd.onrender.com/v1`, OpenAI-compatible, models are OpenRouter slugs such as `openai/gpt-4o`.
- Python SDK: `pip install avaliar-python-sdk`, import `avaliar`, Python 3.11+. Extras: `local`, `otel`, `openai-agents`, `langchain`, `mcp`. `from avaliar import Guard; guard = Guard()` reads `./avaliar.yaml`; checks are `check_input`, `check_output`, `check_tool_call`, `check_tool_result`, `check_action` (async twins `acheck_*`), `check_tool_definitions` and `@guard.tool`. Checks return a `Decision` and never raise, except `AvaliarPolicyError` at construction and the opt-in `GuardBlocked` / `GuardUnavailable`. CLI: `avaliar setup`, `init`, `doctor`, `scan`, `logs`, `stats`, `verify`, `redteam`, `models`, `judge`, `sync`, `detectors`, `policy`. It makes no network calls to Avaliar without `AVALIAR_API_KEY`; with it, evidence records upload and guard traces appear on the dashboard. `@traceable` is now only an optional OpenTelemetry span helper.
- Plans: the Python SDK needs no account. Linking it to the dashboard uses an `sdk`-scoped key; the Avaliar Cloud deep check (`judge.provider: avaliar`) and the Proxy require Pro.

This file is generated from the documentation source. `llms.txt` is the index; `llms-full.txt` contains the complete text of every page.

---

# Introduction

> AI Runtime governance platform that monitors, detects, and provides evidence of AI risk in production

Source: https://docs.avaliar.ai/index  |  Section: Getting Started

Avaliar is an AI runtime governance platform that monitors, detects, and provides evidence of AI risk in production LLM applications. Whether you are dealing with hallucinations, bias, toxicity, PII leaks, or prompt injection attempts, Avaliar provides real-time detection and actionable insights to keep your AI systems safe and reliable.

- [Quickstart](https://docs.avaliar.ai/quickstart): Get up and running with Avaliar in 5 minutes.
- [Python SDK](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/installation): An open-source runtime guard that runs inside your app, offline.
- [Proxy Integration](https://docs.avaliar.ai/proxy/overview): Route LLM traffic through the Avaliar Proxy for zero-code tracing.

## How It Works

Avaliar follows a three-stage lifecycle that takes every LLM interaction from raw data to resolved insight.

### Step 1: Capture

Put the open-source Python SDK guard inside your app, route traffic through the Avaliar Proxy, or send OpenTelemetry data. Every request and response is recorded as a structured trace, and every SDK guard decision as a tamper-evident evidence record.

### Step 2: Detect

Inputs, outputs, tool calls and tool results are checked for safety issues: prompt injection (covering jailbreaks and SQL injection), toxicity, PII and secrets, hallucination, bias, misinformation, misuse, graphic content, illegal activities, and personal safety. The SDK checks in your process, before anything reaches your model; Proxy and OpenTelemetry traffic is checked on Avaliar's backend.

### Step 3: Alert

When a detector finds an issue, Avaliar scores its severity and evaluates it against your alert rules. Notifications are dispatched to your configured channels so your team can investigate and respond immediately.

## Explore the Platform

- [Core Concepts](https://docs.avaliar.ai/concepts): Understand traces, spans, detectors, issues, alerts, and reports: the building blocks of Avaliar.
- [Platform](https://docs.avaliar.ai/platform/traces): Explore the Traces dashboard, analytics, alerts, and reports in the Avaliar platform.

---

# Quickstart

> Start with Avaliar in 5 minutes: the Proxy API, or the open-source Python SDK guard

Source: https://docs.avaliar.ai/quickstart  |  Section: Getting Started

There are **two ways** to put Avaliar in front of your LLM traffic. Pick the one
that fits your stack.

- **Proxy API**: Route your LLM calls through Avaliar's endpoint. **No SDK, no code changes**: swap your provider URL and add your Avaliar key. Works with any language. Best for: quick setup, non-Python apps.
- **Python SDK**: An open-source runtime guard inside your app. It checks every message, tool call and reply against a policy you own, and records every decision. Best for: Python apps and agents, offline or private data, no account.

## Which should I use?

| | Proxy API | Python SDK |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **How you integrate** | Change your endpoint URL | Call the guard's checks, or add one line for your agent framework |
| **Language** | Any (HTTP) | Python 3.11+ |
| **Where checks run** | Avaliar's cloud | Inside your process: rules, local models, an optional deep check |
| **What is checked** | Prompts and responses | Input, output, tool calls, tool results and actions |
| **Blocks prompt injection** | Yes, before it reaches the LLM | Yes, before it reaches your model |
| **Account** | Pro plan | None; an `sdk` key adds your team's dashboard |

> **Tip:** Not sure? In Python, start with the **SDK**: it runs offline with no account,
> and one environment variable links it to the dashboard later. For zero code
> changes or another language, use the **Proxy API**.

---

## Set up your method

The Proxy needs an API key from the [Avaliar Dashboard](https://app.avaliar.ai)
with the `proxy` scope. The SDK needs no key to run; an `sdk` key links it to the
dashboard.

### Proxy API

The proxy exposes an **OpenAI-compatible** endpoint, so any OpenAI SDK or
no-code tool works by just changing the base URL: no provider keys in your
code, no special request shape.

#### Step 1: Create a Proxy API key

1. Open **Settings → API Keys** in the [dashboard](https://app.avaliar.ai/settings/api-keys).
2. Click **Create Key** and select the **`proxy`** scope.
3. Copy the key. You won't be able to see it again.

> **Warning:** Use your Avaliar key only in server-side code. Never expose it in a
> browser or client app.

#### Step 2: Add credits (or bring your own key)

Proxy calls run on **OpenRouter** through Avaliar. To use them you need
either:
- **Credits**: every org starts at **$0**; a workspace admin tops up the
  prepaid balance, **or**
- **Your own OpenRouter key**: add it under **Settings → Organization →
  OpenRouter API Key**. When set, calls bill your OpenRouter account
  directly and credits aren't used.

With no credits and no key, proxy calls return `402 Out of proxy credits`.
See [BYO key & credits](https://docs.avaliar.ai/proxy/openai-compatible#credits-and-byo-key).

#### Step 3: Point any OpenAI client at the proxy

Set three things on your OpenAI-compatible client/tool:
- **Base URL:** `https://proxy-api-ckjd.onrender.com/v1`
- **API key:** your Avaliar **proxy** key (sent as a Bearer token)
- **Model:** an OpenRouter slug, e.g. `openai/gpt-4o`

```python OpenAI SDK (Python)
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://proxy-api-ckjd.onrender.com/v1",
    api_key="your-avaliar-proxy-key",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-4o",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```

```javascript OpenAI SDK (Node)
import OpenAI from "openai";

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "https://proxy-api-ckjd.onrender.com/v1",
  apiKey: "your-avaliar-proxy-key",
});

const resp = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "openai/gpt-4o",
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Hello!" }],
});
```

```bash curl
curl https://proxy-api-ckjd.onrender.com/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer your-avaliar-proxy-key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "openai/gpt-4o",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
  }'
```

> **Info:** Models use OpenRouter slugs (`vendor/model`), such as `openai/gpt-4o`,
> `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`, `google/gemini-2.5-flash`, etc. Find
> them at [openrouter.ai/models](https://openrouter.ai/models). Detection
> runs automatically on every call. Full reference:
> [OpenAI-Compatible Endpoint](https://docs.avaliar.ai/proxy/openai-compatible).

#### Step 4: View in the dashboard

Open [app.avaliar.ai/traces](https://app.avaliar.ai/traces) to see your
traces, detected issues, latency, and cost in real time. A trace
appears within a few seconds of the call.

### Python SDK

#### Step 1: Install the SDK

```bash
pip install "avaliar-python-sdk[local]"
```

Python 3.11 or newer. The `[local]` extra adds the local models; without
it the guard runs on rules alone.

#### Step 2: Write your policy

```bash
avaliar init       # or: avaliar setup, the same questions in your browser
avaliar doctor     # is everything ready?
```

This writes `avaliar.yaml`, the policy your team owns, and `.avaliar/`,
the local evidence log.

#### Step 3: Guard your app

```python
from avaliar import Guard

guard = Guard()                    # reads ./avaliar.yaml

d = guard.check_input(user_message)
if d.blocked:
    return d.reply                 # the policy's reply text
prompt = d.text                    # original, or with [EMAIL_1]-style redactions

answer = call_your_model(prompt)
answer = guard.check_output(answer).text
```

Guard tools with `@guard.tool`, or add one line for the
[OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain or MCP](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/integrations).

#### Step 4: See what happened

```bash
avaliar logs       # every decision
avaliar verify     # check the evidence hash chains
```

Everything so far runs offline and sends nothing anywhere.

#### Step 5: Connect the dashboard (optional)

1. Open **Settings, API Keys** in the [dashboard](https://app.avaliar.ai/settings/api-keys).
2. Click **Create Key** and select the **`sdk`** scope.
3. Set it where your app runs:

```bash macOS / Linux
export AVALIAR_API_KEY="your-key"
```

```powershell Windows (PowerShell)
$env:AVALIAR_API_KEY = "your-key"
```

With no code change, every decision is also uploaded and each request's
checks appear as one trace at
[app.avaliar.ai/traces](https://app.avaliar.ai/traces). See
[Connecting to Avaliar Cloud](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/cloud).

> **Warning:** Store your API key securely. Treat it like a password and never commit
> it to source control.

## Next Steps

- [Proxy Integration](https://docs.avaliar.ai/proxy/overview): Full proxy reference: supported models, confidential mode, and the request pipeline.
- [SDK quickstart](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/quickstart): The full first run: policy, checks, tools, the deep check and red-teaming.
- [Detection](https://docs.avaliar.ai/detection/overview): The detectors, where they run, and severity levels.

# Core Concepts

> The key building blocks of Avaliar. Read this before diving into the detailed guides

Source: https://docs.avaliar.ai/concepts  |  Section: Getting Started

Avaliar is built around a small set of core primitives. This page gives you a quick mental model of each concept. Each section links to the full documentation where you can go deeper.

## Traces

A **trace** represents a single LLM interaction from input to output. Traces are the fundamental unit of observability in Avaliar. Every request routed through the Proxy or sent over OpenTelemetry creates a trace that captures the full request-response lifecycle, including the prompt, completion, model, provider, latency, token counts, and any detected issues. With the Python SDK linked to Avaliar Cloud, the guard checks of one request (input, tool calls, tool results, output) share a trace id and appear as one guard trace.

Traces are stored in your organization's workspace and visible in the [Traces dashboard](https://app.avaliar.ai/traces). You can filter, search, and inspect them to understand how your LLM application behaves in production.

→ [Traces on the Platform](https://docs.avaliar.ai/platform/traces)

## Spans

**Spans** are individual operations within a trace. A trace can contain multiple nested spans in a parent-child hierarchy, letting you see exactly how a complex LLM pipeline executes step by step.

Avaliar supports four span types:

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `llm` | A direct call to a language model |
| `tool` | A tool or function call made by the model |
| `agent` | An autonomous agent step that may contain child spans |
| `generic` | Any other operation you want to track |

Nesting spans lets you trace multi-step workflows such as RAG pipelines, agent loops, or chain-of-thought sequences. Parent-child relationships are tracked automatically, with no manual wiring.

→ [OpenTelemetry ingestion](https://docs.avaliar.ai/otlp/overview) · [SDK OpenTelemetry spans](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/opentelemetry)

## Detection

**Detection** is the automated analysis of traces for safety issues. Avaliar provides ten built-in detectors:

| Detector | What It Finds |
|----------|---------------|
| **Prompt Injection** | Attempts to override system instructions via user input. Also covers jailbreak and SQL-injection patterns in a single pass (runs synchronously as a pre-LLM blocking gate) |
| **Toxicity** | Harmful, abusive, or offensive language in inputs or outputs |
| **PII** | Personally identifiable information: emails, phone numbers, SSNs, etc. |
| **Bias** | Stereotyping, demographic bias, or unfair treatment in model outputs |
| **Hallucination** | Factually incorrect or fabricated information in model responses |
| **Misinformation** | Verifiably false claims: conspiracy content, fabricated advice |
| **Misuse** | Attempts to weaponize the model: phishing, malware, fraud |
| **Graphic Content** | Explicit violence or sexual content that breaches content-safety standards |
| **Illegal Activities** | Requests for dangerous or unlawful instructional content |
| **Personal Safety** | Self-harm encouragement, dangerous advice, radicalization |

Detection runs in one of two places: **in your process**, with the open-source Python SDK guard (nothing leaves your infrastructure unless you choose), or **on Avaliar's backend**, for Proxy and OpenTelemetry traffic.

→ [Detection Overview](https://docs.avaliar.ai/detection/overview) · [Detector Reference](https://docs.avaliar.ai/detection/detectors) · [Where detection runs](https://docs.avaliar.ai/detection/modes) · [SDK categories](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/detection)

## Issues

An **issue** is a finding produced by a detector during trace analysis. Each issue contains:

- **Type**: the detector that found it (e.g., `toxicity`, `pii`)
- **Severity**: one of `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`
- **Confidence**: a score from 0 to 1 indicating certainty
- **Description**: a human-readable explanation of the finding
- **Excerpt**: the specific portion of the input or output that triggered detection

Issues are attached to their parent trace and visible in both the trace detail view and the aggregated Issues section of the dashboard.

## Guard, policy and evidence

The open-source **Python SDK** is a runtime guard inside your app. At five **checkpoints** (input, output, tool call, tool result, action) it checks the text or call, **decides** by a policy file your team owns (`avaliar.yaml`), and **records** every decision in a hash-chained local evidence log you can verify with `avaliar verify`.

| Action | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| `allow` / `warn` | The check passes; findings are recorded |
| `redact` | Personal data and secrets are replaced with placeholders such as `[EMAIL_1]` |
| `block` | The policy's reply is returned instead |
| `approve` | A person must approve the tool call or action first |

It runs offline with no account. Setting `AVALIAR_API_KEY` uploads the evidence so guard traces appear on the dashboard.

→ [SDK installation](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/installation) · [Guard and decisions](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/guard) · [Policy file](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/policy) · [Evidence and verify](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/evidence)

## Alerts

**Alerts** are automated notifications triggered when issues meet conditions you define. Each alert rule specifies:

- **Condition type**: `threshold` (count exceeds N), `trend` (rate increasing), `pattern` (repeated issue type), or `anomaly` (statistical outlier)
- **Channels**: where to send the notification: email, Slack, or webhook

You can scope alerts to specific detectors, severity levels, models, or environments. Full alert history is stored and available for auditing.

→ [Alerts on the Platform](https://docs.avaliar.ai/platform/alerts)

## Reports

**Reports** are generated documents that aggregate trace data, issues, and benchmark results into a structured format for compliance and stakeholder review.

| Report | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| **Security Risk** | Detected threats, attack patterns, and mitigation status |
| **Model Cost** | Token usage, latency, and spend by model and provider |
| **Platform Ops** | System health, uptime, trace volume, and error rates |
| **AI Risk Posture** | Overall safety score combining detection, benchmark, and eval results |

Reports can be generated on-demand or scheduled, and exported as PDF or JSON.

→ [Reports on the Platform](https://docs.avaliar.ai/platform/reports)

---

# Installation

> Install the Avaliar Python SDK, an open-source runtime guard for AI apps and agents

Source: https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/installation  |  Section: Python SDK

The Avaliar Python SDK is an open-source runtime guard. It runs inside your process and, at every risky point of your app or agent, it does three things:

1. **Checks** the text, tool call or action: rules, local models, and an optional deep check for the uncertain cases.
2. **Decides** by a policy file your team owns (`avaliar.yaml`).
3. **Records** every decision in a tamper-evident local log you can verify.

It works fully offline with no account. Without an API key it makes no network calls to Avaliar.

## Requirements

Python **3.11** or newer (3.14 is supported).

## Install

```bash
pip install avaliar-python-sdk
```

The package installs as `avaliar-python-sdk`; you import it as `avaliar` and run it as the `avaliar` command.

The base install gives you the rules (tier 0), the policy file, the evidence log and the CLI. It depends only on `pydantic`, `orjson`, `pyyaml` and `requests`, and `import avaliar` loads none of them until you use them.

## Extras

| Extra | Install | Adds |
|---|---|---|
| `local` | `pip install "avaliar-python-sdk[local]"` | Local ONNX models on CPU (tier 1): prompt injection and toxicity, plus jailbreak, names and addresses, off topic and groundedness models fetched with `avaliar models pull` |
| `otel` | `pip install "avaliar-python-sdk[otel]"` | An OpenTelemetry span for every check and for every `@traceable` function. See [OpenTelemetry](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/opentelemetry). |
| `openai-agents` | `pip install "avaliar-python-sdk[openai-agents]"` | `protect()` and `run()` for the OpenAI Agents SDK |
| `langchain` | `pip install "avaliar-python-sdk[langchain]"` | `AvaliarMiddleware` for LangChain 1.x agents |
| `mcp` | `pip install "avaliar-python-sdk[mcp]"` | `GuardedSession` for MCP clients |

Extras combine: `pip install "avaliar-python-sdk[local,otel,langchain]"`.

> **Note:** Nothing downloads at runtime. Model files come with the `[local]` extra or from an explicit `avaliar models pull`, and are checked against pinned sha256 hashes. The local deep check (Clef-Flash, 5.4 GB) is fetched only when you ask for it by name.

## Check the install

```bash
avaliar --version
avaliar doctor
```

`avaliar doctor` checks the Python version, the policy, the local models, the deep check, the evidence log and the machine, and tells you what is missing. See the [Quickstart](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/quickstart) for the full first run.

## Environment variables

None are required. These change where the SDK looks or what it does:

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `AVALIAR_POLICY` | `./avaliar.yaml` | Path to the policy file when `Guard()` is given none |
| `AVALIAR_HOME` | the policy file's folder | Base folder for evidence paths and the per-install secret |
| `AVALIAR_APP` | none | App name written on every evidence record (`app:` in the policy wins) |
| `AVALIAR_MODELS_DIR` | none | Extra folder to look for local model files in |
| `AVALIAR_ONNX_THREADS` | `2` | Threads per local model |
| `AVALIAR_LLAMA_SERVER` | the pinned install, then `PATH` | The `llama-server` binary for the local deep check |
| `AVALIAR_API_KEY` | none | Links the SDK to Avaliar Cloud. See [Connecting to Avaliar Cloud](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/cloud). |
| `AVALIAR_API_URL` | `https://api.avaliar.ai/api/v1` | Avaliar Cloud address, used only when `AVALIAR_API_KEY` is set |
| `AVALIAR_TIMEOUT` | `10` | Seconds to wait for Avaliar Cloud |
| `AVALIAR_NO_TIPS` | off | Hide the tips the CLI prints |

Deep check providers read their own key variables (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` and so on). See [Deep check](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/deep-check).

## Logging

The SDK logs to the `avaliar` logger. It warns once about problems that need you (a policy warning, evidence that cannot be written, a deep check that is unreachable) and never raises from a check. `avaliar -v <command>` prints SDK activity on the command line.

```python
import logging
logging.getLogger("avaliar").setLevel(logging.INFO)
```

## Next steps

- [Quickstart](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/quickstart): Write a policy, check your first message, read the log.
- [Guard and decisions](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/guard): The `Guard` class and the `Decision` it returns.
- [Policy file](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/policy): Presets, rules, actions and every key in `avaliar.yaml`.
- [What leaves your machine](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/network): Every network call the SDK can make, and when.

# SDK quickstart

> Write a policy, guard your first message and read the evidence log, offline, in about five minutes

Source: https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/quickstart  |  Section: Python SDK

This walks through a first run with no account and no network calls. You need Python 3.11 or newer.

## Step 1: Install

```bash
pip install "avaliar-python-sdk[local]"
```

The `[local]` extra adds the local models. Without it the guard runs on rules alone. See [Installation](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/installation) for every extra.

## Step 2: Write the policy

Pick one of two ways to answer the same two questions (local models, an API, or both, and which API):

```bash
avaliar setup     # a page on 127.0.0.1 in your browser: choose, try it, write the files
avaliar init      # the same questions in the terminal
```

Both write `avaliar.yaml` next to your code and create `.avaliar/` (the evidence log and a per-install secret, added to `.gitignore`). In CI, pass the answers as flags:

```bash
avaliar init --how local --no-deep-check --yes
avaliar init --how both --provider anthropic --yes
```

## Step 3: Check the install

```bash
avaliar doctor            # policy, models, deep check, evidence, hardware
avaliar doctor --measure  # also time every installed model on this machine
```

## Step 4: Try a check from the terminal

```bash
avaliar scan "My card is 4539 1488 0343 6467"
```

`scan` runs one check and prints every finding, the decision and the redacted text. Add `--checkpoint output` to check a reply instead, or `--json` for machine output.

## Step 5: Guard your app

```python
from avaliar import Guard

guard = Guard()                    # reads ./avaliar.yaml

d = guard.check_input(user_message)
if d.blocked:
    return d.reply                 # the policy's reply text
prompt = d.text                    # original, or with [EMAIL_1]-style redactions

answer = call_your_model(prompt)
answer = guard.check_output(answer).text
```

Send `d.text` to your model, not the original message, so redactions take effect. A check never raises: it returns a [`Decision`](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/guard#the-decision).

## Step 6: Guard your tools

```python
@guard.tool
def send_email(to: str, body: str) -> str: ...

docs = guard.check_tool_result("search", search(query)).text
```

`@guard.tool` checks every call before the tool runs and its result before the model reads it. `check_tool_result` does the same for content your app fetches itself, which is where indirect prompt injection arrives.

## Step 7: See what happened

```bash
avaliar logs            # every decision, newest last
avaliar stats           # counts by action, category and tier
avaliar verify          # check the evidence hash chains
```

## Add a deep check (optional)

Rules and local models settle most messages in milliseconds. For the few they are unsure about, and for categories no local model covers (harmful content, your own rules), add a deep check. To keep everything on this machine:

```bash
avaliar judge install     # a pinned llama.cpp server and Clef-Flash (5.4 GB, sha256 checked)
avaliar judge start       # runs on 127.0.0.1:8080 in the background
```

Or use an API you already have a key for. See [Deep check](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/deep-check).

## Attack your own app (optional)

```bash
avaliar redteam --target myapp:reply
```

This sends the bundled attack pack, and harmless look-alikes, through your real app. See [Red-team](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/redteam).

## Next steps

- [Checkpoints](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/checkpoints/input): Where to call each of the five checks.
- [Policy file](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/policy): Change what blocks, redacts, warns or asks for approval.
- [Framework integrations](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/integrations): One line for OpenAI Agents, LangChain and MCP.
- [Connect to Avaliar Cloud](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/cloud): See guard traces on your team's dashboard.

---

# Guard and decisions

> The Guard class, the five checks, the Decision they return, context, approvals and async

Source: https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/guard  |  Section: Python SDK

A `Guard` holds one policy and runs the checks. Create it once, at startup, and reuse it: it keeps its models, its evidence writer and its per-session memory between calls.

```python
from avaliar import Guard

guard = Guard()                                     # $AVALIAR_POLICY, else ./avaliar.yaml, else the recommended preset
guard = Guard("policies/prod.yaml")                 # an explicit file
guard = Guard(policy={"version": 1, "extends": "strict"})   # a dict
```

An invalid policy raises `AvaliarPolicyError` here, with the file, line and key. It is the only error a guard raises on its own. See [Error handling](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/error-handling).

> **Note:** Without a policy file the guard runs the `recommended` preset and records nothing. Run `avaliar init` to write `avaliar.yaml` and turn on the evidence log.

## Constructor

```python
Guard(
    source=None,              # path to a policy file
    *,
    policy=None,              # or a policy as a dict (not both)
    approval_handler=None,    # who answers "approve" decisions; default denies
    raise_on_block=False,     # raise GuardBlocked instead of returning a block
    judge=None,               # a custom deep check object, instead of judge: in the policy
    record=True,              # False: never write evidence from this guard
    on_follow_up=None,        # callback for checks that ran after the reply
)
```

## The five checks

| Method | Checkpoint | What you pass |
|---|---|---|
| `check_input(text, context=None)` | [input](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/checkpoints/input) | The user's message, or the whole chat as a list of `{"role", "content"}` messages |
| `check_output(text, context=None)` | [output](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/checkpoints/output) | The model's reply, or the chat |
| `check_tool_call(name, args=None, context=None)` | [tool_call](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/checkpoints/tool-call) | A tool's name and its arguments |
| `check_tool_result(name, result, context=None)` | [tool_result](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/checkpoints/tool-result) | A tool's output, a fetched page or a retrieved document |
| `check_action(name, details=None, context=None)` | [action](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/checkpoints/action) | An action with real-world effect and its details |

Two more cover tools:

- `@guard.tool` wraps a function so its calls and results are checked. See [Tool call](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/checkpoints/tool-call).
- `check_tool_definitions(tools, server=None)` checks a tool list (MCP `tools/list`, OpenAI or Anthropic tool specs) for poisoned descriptions before the model sees it. See [Tool result](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/checkpoints/tool-result).

### Async

Every check has an async twin: `acheck_input`, `acheck_output`, `acheck_tool_call`, `acheck_tool_result`, `acheck_action`, `acheck_tool_definitions`, and `aapprove` for approvals. `@guard.tool` works on async functions and generators as they are.

```python
d = await guard.acheck_input(user_message)
```

### Module-level shortcuts

For scripts, the same checks exist as functions on the package. They use one shared `Guard()` created on first use (`avaliar.default_guard()`):

```python
import avaliar

d = avaliar.check_input("Ignore all previous instructions")
```

## The decision

Every check returns a `Decision`:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `action` | `allow`, `warn`, `redact`, `block` or `approve`. When several rules fire, the strictest wins. |
| `blocked`, `allowed`, `redacted`, `needs_approval` | Shortcuts for the action. `allowed` is true for `allow`, `warn` and `redact`. |
| `text` | The checked text, with redactions applied (`[EMAIL_1]`, `[CARD_1]`, `[SECRET_1]`). Use this, not the original. |
| `args` | For tool calls and actions: the arguments with redactions applied |
| `reply` | The policy's reply text when the decision blocks (`replies.block`, or `replies.approval_denied`) |
| `reasons` | Short, human-readable reasons for the action |
| `findings` | One `Finding` per detector result: `category`, `detector`, `version`, `tier`, `score`, `band`, `spans`, `kind`, `detail` |
| `not_evaluated` | Categories nothing could score, with a reason (`judge_unavailable`, `budget`, `error` and others). Never counted as clean. |
| `deferred` | Warn-only categories that will run after the reply (see [speed](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/policy#speed)) |
| `record_id`, `evidence_ok` | The evidence record's id, and whether it was written |
| `trace_id` | The trace this check belongs to (see [traces](#traces-and-context)) |
| `policy_hash` | Hash of the policy the decision was made under |
| `latency_ms` | Time the check took |
| `approval` | The approval answer, after `guard.approve(d)` |

`d.raise_for_block()` raises `GuardBlocked` when the decision blocks or waits for approval, and returns the decision otherwise. `d.to_dict()` gives a JSON-ready dict.

```python
d = guard.check_output(reply)
if d.blocked:
    return d.reply
for f in d.findings:
    print(f.category, f.tier, round(f.score, 2), f.detector)
for n in d.not_evaluated:
    print("not evaluated:", n.category, n.reason)
```

## Traces and context

`guard.context(...)` attaches values to every check inside the block. Wrap each request in it:

```python
with guard.context(session_id=conversation.id, user_id=user.id, agent="support", tenant="acme", tags={"env": "prod"}):
    d = guard.check_input(message)
    ...
    guard.check_output(reply)
```

| Key | Used for |
|---|---|
| `session_id` | Per-session memory for `tool misuse.taint` and `tool misuse.loops` |
| `user_id` | Stored only as a keyed fingerprint (`user_id_hash`), never in clear |
| `agent` | The agent's name on the evidence record |
| `tenant` | Picks one customer's [examples](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/examples) |
| `tags` | Free-form labels on the evidence record |
| `trace_id` | Your own trace id for every check in the block |

Each check also takes `context=` for values that apply to that check only, such as `{"retrieval_context": docs}` for hallucination or `{"system_prompt": prompt}` for data leak.

Every decision carries a `trace_id`, so one request's input, tool and output checks group into one trace. The id comes from `guard.context(trace_id=...)` when you set it, else from your app's current OpenTelemetry trace, else one is made per request turn. The outermost `guard.context()` block starts a new turn, so checks on a reused worker thread never join a previous request's trace.

## Approvals

A rule with `action: approve` returns a decision that waits for a person. Pass a handler that knows how to reach one:

```python
from avaliar import Approval, ApprovalRequest, Guard

def ask_slack(req: ApprovalRequest) -> Approval:
    ok = post_and_wait(f"Approve {req.name} {req.details}? Reasons: {req.reasons}")
    return Approval(ok, approver="ops-oncall")

guard = Guard(approval_handler=ask_slack)

d = guard.check_action("refund", {"amount": 420, "order": order_id})
if d.needs_approval:
    d = guard.approve(d)        # allow when approved, block when not
d.raise_for_block()
```

The handler gets an `ApprovalRequest` (`checkpoint`, `name`, `details`, `text`, `reasons`, `decision_id`, `context`) and returns a `bool` or an `Approval(approved, approver=None, note=None)`. It may be async. The answer is written to the evidence log, linked to the decision.

Without a handler every approval is denied and recorded as `approval_unavailable`. For local development, `avaliar.approval.console` asks on the terminal. `@guard.tool` and the framework integrations call the handler for you.

## Lifecycle

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `guard.warmup()` | Load the local models now instead of on the first check |
| `guard.flush(timeout=5.0)` | Wait for after-the-reply checks, pending evidence writes and, with a key, a short upload |
| `guard.close()` | Flush and stop background work |
| `guard.add_examples(category, flag=..., allow=..., tenant=None)` | Teach the guard your own examples. See [Your own examples](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/examples). |
| `guard.policy_hash` | Hash of the loaded policy |

Evidence is written off the request path and flushed at exit. In serverless handlers, call `guard.flush()` before returning, since the process is frozen rather than exited.

---

# Policy file

> avaliar.yaml: presets, rules, actions, budgets, the deep check, evidence and speed

Source: https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/policy  |  Section: Python SDK

What to check, and what to do about it, lives in one file your team owns: `avaliar.yaml`. Every decision records the hash of the policy it was made under, so you can always show which rules were in force.

`Guard()` looks for the policy in this order: the path you pass, `$AVALIAR_POLICY`, `./avaliar.yaml` (or `.yml`), and otherwise the built-in `recommended` preset with evidence off. `avaliar init` and `avaliar setup` write a starting file for you.

## A first policy

```yaml
version: 1
extends: recommended          # or strict, minimal, or a path to another policy

judge:
  provider: local             # local | jev | anthropic | openai | gemini | groq | openrouter | avaliar | none

input:
  budget_ms: 300
  on_error: fail_open
  rules:
    prompt injection: { action: block, threshold: 0.8 }
    sensitive data:   { action: redact }

tool_call:
  rules:
    tools:
      send_email: { action: approve }
      run_sql:    { deny_args: { query: ["(?i)\\bdrop\\b"] } }
```

Unknown keys are errors with line numbers. Check a file before you ship it:

```bash
avaliar policy check            # validate ./avaliar.yaml
avaliar policy show             # the resolved policy (presets merged in) and its hash
```

The JSON Schema is `schema/policy.v1.json` in the SDK repository, for editor completion and CI.

## Presets

| Preset | What it does |
|---|---|
| `recommended` | Blocks prompt injection and hidden text on input and tool results, redacts personal data, blocks leaked secrets, toxic replies and data leaks, asks for approval on dangerous tool arguments. Fails open. Fast path on (`speed`). |
| `strict` | Lower thresholds, more categories blocked, every action needs approval, evidence is required, every checkpoint fails closed, every local model runs on every check. |
| `minimal` | Blocks clear prompt injection and leaked secrets, asks before dangerous tool arguments. Records no text. |

`extends` merges per key: fields of `judge`, `evidence`, `replies` and `speed` override one by one; a rule replaces the preset's rule of the same name at the same checkpoint; `null` removes it; tool and action rules merge per name; `examples` merge per category.

```yaml
version: 1
extends: recommended
output:
  rules:
    harmful content: null        # drop the preset's rule
    toxicity: { action: warn }   # replace it
```

## Actions

| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| `allow` | Nothing happens; the finding is recorded |
| `warn` | The decision is allowed and the finding is recorded as a warning |
| `redact` | Matched spans are replaced with numbered placeholders (`[EMAIL_1]`, `[CARD_1]`, `[SECRET_1]`) in `d.text` and `d.args` |
| `block` | `d.blocked` is true and `d.reply` holds the policy's reply |
| `approve` | The decision waits for a person (`guard.approve(d)`); denied without an approval handler |

When several rules fire, the strictest wins.

## Top-level keys

`version` (required, `1`), `extends`, `app`, `judge`, `evidence`, `speed`, one section per checkpoint (`input`, `output`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `action`), `replies`, `detectors`, `examples`.

`app` names the app on every evidence record (else `$AVALIAR_APP`).

## Checkpoints

One section per checkpoint.

| Key | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `budget_ms` | int | input 300, output 1500, tool_call 300, tool_result 1000, action 300 |
| `on_error` | `fail_open` or `fail_closed` | `fail_open` |
| `scan.roles` | list of `system`, `user`, `assistant`, `tool`, `developer` | input: `user`, output: `assistant` |
| `scan.last_only` | bool | `true` |
| `rules` | map of category to rule, plus `tools` or `actions` | `{}` |

`on_error` decides what happens when a category could not be evaluated (a model failed, the deep check timed out, the budget ran out): `fail_open` decides from what could be scored and records the gap as `not_evaluated`; `fail_closed` blocks when the category's rule would block or ask for approval. `scan` picks which chat messages are read when you pass a list of messages.

### Category rules

A rule under `<checkpoint>.rules.<category>`. Category names may use spaces or underscores (`prompt injection` or `prompt_injection`), and a part of a category is written after a dot (`sensitive data.secrets`).

| Key | Type | Applies to |
|---|---|---|
| `action` | `allow`, `warn`, `redact`, `block`, `approve` | every rule (required) |
| `threshold` | float, 0 to 1 | every rule; defaults per category |
| `topics` | list | `off topic` (required) |
| `allowed` | list of language codes | `language` (required) |
| `terms`, `patterns` | lists | `blocklist` (one of them required) |
| `criteria` | string | `custom.<name>` (required) |
| `allow_domains`, `canaries` | lists | `data leak` |
| `allow_hosts`, `trusted_tools`, `max_calls`, `max_repeats`, `window_s` | lists and numbers | `tool misuse` |

A rule on a category acts on its highest-scoring part; a rule on a part acts on that part alone, so secrets can block while personal data is only redacted. Options can sit on the category or on any of its parts. See [Detectors and categories](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/detection) for what each category catches.

### Tool and action rules

Under `tool_call.rules.tools` and `action.rules.actions`, keyed by exact name or glob. The exact name wins, then the longest glob.

| Key | Type | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `action` | `allow`, `warn`, `block`, `approve` | Applies when no argument rule blocks |
| `deny_args` | map of argument to list of regexes | Any match blocks |
| `allow_args` | map of argument to list of regexes | An argument that is missing or matches nothing blocks |

The `recommended` and `strict` presets allow every tool (`"*": {action: allow}`); `strict` also asks for approval on every action. Name the tools and actions that need a person or must never run.

## `judge`

The deep check for what rules and local models could not settle. See [Deep check](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/deep-check).

| Key | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `provider` | `local`, `jev`, `anthropic`, `openai`, `gemini`, `groq`, `openrouter`, `avaliar`, `none` | `none` |
| `model` | string | the provider's default |
| `api_key_env` | string | the provider's usual variable |
| `base_url` | string | the provider's address |
| `timeout_ms` | int | `5000` |
| `within_budget` | bool | `false` |
| `min_budget_ms` | int | `200` |
| `breaker_failures` | int | `5` |
| `breaker_cooldown_s` | float | `30.0` |

## `evidence`

The local evidence log. Paths are relative to the policy file (or `$AVALIAR_HOME`). See [Evidence and verify](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/evidence).

| Key | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool | `true` |
| `path` | string | `.avaliar/evidence` |
| `capture` | `none`, `redacted`, `full` | `redacted` |
| `required` | bool | `false` |
| `rotate_mb` | int | `100` |

## `speed`

How hard the guard works on the request path.

| Key | Values | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deep_models` | `when_unsure`, `always` | `when_unsure` | `when_unsure` runs the bigger local models (GLiNER, Wolf, TinyLettuce) only for categories the quick models could not settle, so clean messages stay fast |
| `warn_after_reply` | bool | `false` | Categories whose rules at a checkpoint only `warn` run after the decision is returned, on a background thread, and are written as `follow_up` records |

The `recommended` preset turns both fast paths on (`when_unsure`, `warn_after_reply: true`); `strict` runs every model inline. `Decision.deferred` lists the categories that will run later, `Guard(on_follow_up=...)` receives their results, and `guard.flush()` waits for them. Measured with every model installed, a clean 20-word message takes about 2.5 ms with the fast path instead of 11 ms.

## `replies`

| Key | Default |
|---|---|
| `block` | `Sorry, I can't help with that.` |
| `approval_denied` | `This action was not approved.` |

The text returned in `Decision.reply`.

## `detectors`

Per-detector switches and uncertainty bands, under `detectors.<detector name>` (names come from `avaliar detectors`):

| Key | Type | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool | Turn one detector off |
| `allow_below` | float | Scores below this are settled as clean |
| `block_at` | float | Scores at or above this are settled as flagged |

Scores between `allow_below` and `block_at` are the uncertain band that goes to the deep check.

## `examples`

Your own `flag` and `allow` examples per category, optionally per tenant. See [Your own examples](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/examples).

---

# Detectors and categories

> The sixteen categories, the detectors behind each, and the tiers that score them

Source: https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/detection  |  Section: Python SDK

The guard sorts what it finds into sixteen categories. A policy rule names a category (or one of its parts) and says what to do. `avaliar detectors` lists every category with its short name, its checkpoints, its options and what it needs.

## Tiers

| Tier | What | Cost | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Rules: injection payloads, jailbreak templates, personal data, secrets, hidden text, leaks, tool arguments, taint, loops, word lists, language | about 1 ms | nothing |
| 1 | Local ONNX models: prompt injection and toxicity (in the wheel); jailbreaks, names and addresses, off topic, groundedness (`avaliar models pull`) | about 5 to 50 ms on CPU, more for long text | `[local]` extra |
| 2 | The [deep check](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/deep-check), only for what tiers 0 and 1 are unsure about: Clef-Flash on this machine, or an API (Jev, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter, any OpenAI-compatible URL, or Avaliar Cloud) | seconds on a laptop CPU locally; about 0.5 to 1 s by API | the model file, or your key |

Without a deep check the local score is final, so the offline guard still blocks. A category nothing could score is reported as `not_evaluated`, never as clean.

> **Warning:** Without a deep check, harmful content and your own `custom` rules are not evaluated at all. `avaliar stats` shows how often a category was not evaluated.

## The categories

Write them in a policy with spaces or underscores (`prompt injection` or `prompt_injection`). Evidence records use the underscore form.

| Category | Parts you can set separately | Checkpoints | Rules (tier 0) | Local model (tier 1) | Deep check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| prompt injection | | input, tool_result | injection payloads, jailbreak templates, poisoned tool descriptions | StackOne Defender; Wolf Defender Edge (input) | yes |
| sensitive data | `personal`, `secrets` | all | PII patterns with checksums; API keys, tokens, passwords | GLiNER pii-edge (names, addresses, health, salary) | yes |
| toxicity | | input, output, tool_result | | MiniLMv2 toxic-jigsaw | yes |
| harmful content | `bias`, `misinformation`, `misuse`, `graphic_content`, `illegal_activities`, `personal_safety`, `advice` | input, output, tool_result | | | only |
| hallucination | | output | | TinyLettuce 17M (needs `retrieval_context`) | yes |
| hidden text | | all | Unicode tags, bidi controls, zero-width runs, lookalike letters | | |
| data leak | `links`, `system_prompt` | output, tool_call | data in links and images; canaries and a copied system prompt | | |
| tool misuse | `args`, `taint`, `loops` | tool_call, action | dangerous arguments; values from untrusted tool output; loops and call budgets | | |
| off topic | | input, output | | potion-base-8M | yes (gets your topics) |
| language | | input, output | writing system plus common words, 16 Latin-script languages | | |
| gibberish | | input, output | keyboard mash, floods, random strings | | word salad |
| blocklist | | all | your terms and regexes | | |
| copyright | | output | licence and confidentiality notices | | copied prose |
| `custom.<name>` | | all | | | only |
| tools | | tool_call | your allow and deny rules | | |
| actions | | action | your approval rules | | |

Every category except tools and actions also takes your own `flag` and `allow` examples, which beat the models. See [Your own examples](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/examples).

## Turning them on

The `recommended` preset runs the categories that need no setup. Add the rest in your policy:

```yaml
version: 1
extends: recommended

input:
  rules:
    off topic: { action: block, topics: ["billing questions", "card and account support"] }
    language:  { action: block, allowed: [en, es] }
    gibberish: { action: warn }

output:
  rules:
    sensitive data:          { action: redact }
    sensitive data.secrets:  { action: block }
    data leak:               { action: block, canaries: ["avl-3f9c1e07b2d84a65"] }
    blocklist:               { action: redact, terms: [Project Falcon], patterns: ['\bTKT-\d{5}\b'] }
    harmful content.advice:  { action: warn }
    custom.no_competitors:
      action: block
      criteria: "The reply recommends or praises a competitor's product"

tool_call:
  rules:
    tool misuse.args:  { action: approve, allow_hosts: [billing.internal] }
    tool misuse.taint: { action: approve, trusted_tools: ["crm_*", "saved_payees"] }
    tool misuse.loops: { action: block, max_repeats: 3, max_calls: 50, window_s: 600 }
```

## Notes by category

### prompt injection

Runs on every `tool_result`, so poisoned MCP tool descriptions are caught there too. Use `guard.check_tool_definitions(tools)` to check a server's tool list before the model sees it. The jailbreak and tool-description rules abstain when nothing matches, so the models still read the text.

### sensitive data

With `redact`, personal data becomes `[EMAIL_1]`, `[CARD_1]`, `[NAME_1]` and secrets become `[SECRET_1]`. The GLiNER model adds names and addresses the patterns cannot see; a lone name stays below the block threshold unless it comes with another personal detail.

### hidden text

Decodes Unicode tag text into the finding so a reviewer can read what was hidden. Flag emoji for England, Scotland and Wales, emoji joiners, Persian and Indic joiners, a leading byte order mark, isolates around right-to-left names, and units such as `kΩ` or `μF` are left alone.

### data leak

`data leak.system_prompt` needs something to compare against: plant a marker with `avaliar.new_canary()` and list it under `canaries` (or pass it as context `canary`), or pass the prompt as context `system_prompt`. It also finds a marker that was spaced out or base64-encoded. Translations and paraphrases are beyond it. Without either, only the link rules answer.

### tool misuse

`taint` and `loops` keep per-session memory, keyed by `session_id`:

```python
with guard.context(session_id=conversation.id):
    guard.check_input(user_message)
    ...
```

Taint keeps only salted hashes of emails, URLs, IBANs, phone numbers and wallet addresses, in memory, for an hour. Values the user typed are trusted, and so is output from `trusted_tools`; other tool output is not.

`args` treats a search query or ticket body that mentions `rm -rf /` or `169.254.169.254` as prose and does not fire on it. It decodes URL-encoded paths and only counts `../` that climbs out of where it starts.

### language

Needs no model. Short messages are clear.

### harmful content.advice and custom

Deep check only. Without a deep check they are `not_evaluated`, and `on_error: fail_closed` blocks on that.

## Accuracy

Measured precision, recall and false positive rates per category and checkpoint, for rules alone and for rules plus local models, are generated from a reviewed labelled set and published in the SDK repository (`docs/accuracy.md`). The rule detectors were tuned while looking at those cases, so their rows overstate accuracy on new data. Measure on your own traffic with `avaliar redteam` (see [Red-team](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/redteam)) before relying on a category to block.

## Local models

```bash
avaliar models list          # what is installed, with licences
avaliar models pull          # every downloadable model (sha256 checked)
avaliar models pull potion-base-8M
```

Files go to `~/.cache/avaliar`. Clef-Flash, the local deep check, is pulled only by name (`avaliar models pull clef-flash`, or `avaliar judge install`).

---

# Your own examples

> Teach a category what counts for your business, and what does not, without retraining

Source: https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/examples  |  Section: Python SDK

Models miss things that matter to one business and flag things that are fine for another. Examples fix both: give a category texts that must count (`flag`) and texts that must not (`allow`), and the guard uses them at every tier.

## In the policy file

```yaml
version: 1
extends: recommended

examples:
  toxicity:
    flag:  ["you lot are vermin", "go back to your village"]
    allow: ["this track is sick", "that exam murdered me"]
  sensitive data.personal:
    flag:  ["member number MBR"]
    file:  examples/members.yaml        # more examples, from a file
  harmful content.advice:
    flag:  ["double your dose if the pain comes back"]
    similarity: 0.85                    # stricter near-copy matching
    tenants:
      acme: { allow: ["take two tablets with water"] }   # one customer only
```

- A category (or one of its parts, such as `sensitive data.personal`) needs a rule at a checkpoint for its examples to act there.
- `file` is read when the policy loads, relative to the policy file: `.txt` (one flag example per line, `#` for comments), `.yaml` (`flag:` and `allow:` lists) or `.jsonl` (`{"text": "...", "flag": false}` per line). Its contents count toward the policy hash.
- `extends` merges examples per category: a child's set for a category replaces the parent's.
- Every category except tools and actions takes examples.

## From code

For examples that live in your own database, or that your customers manage in your product:

```python
guard.add_examples("toxicity", flag=["you lot are vermin"], allow=["this track is sick"])
guard.add_examples("sensitive data.personal", flag=["MBR-"], tenant="acme")

with guard.context(tenant="acme"):      # acme's examples apply here
    guard.check_input(message)
```

Examples without a tenant apply to everyone; tenant examples apply only to checks whose context carries that `tenant`, so one customer's rules never affect another's. An unknown category raises `AvaliarPolicyError`.

## How they are used

| Tier | What happens | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Rules (0) | Text and examples are normalised (case, spacing, punctuation, zero-width and lookalike characters, leetspeak like `l0t`). A flag example inside the text, or text that is a near copy of one, flags the category. Text that is a near copy of an allow example clears it. | nothing |
| Meaning (1) | Each sentence is compared with every flag example by embedding similarity. 0.85 or more flags; 0.65 to 0.85 is uncertain and goes to the deep check. Text 0.9 or more from an allow example clears the category. | `potion-base-8M` (`avaliar models pull potion-base-8M`) |
| Deep check (2) | The examples closest to the text are sent with the request as the operator's word on what counts. | a deep check |

**An allow example beats every detector.** If a model flags something you have marked as fine, the allow match wins and the decision says why (`matches your allow#2 example`). A flag example does not need to beat anything: it adds a finding, and the rule's action and threshold decide.

`allow` matches near copies only, never containment, so allowing "this track is sick" does not allow "this track is sick and you are vermin". With `redact`, a matched flag example becomes `[REDACTED_1]` when its place in the text can be found.

## Evidence

Every evidence record carries the hash of the example set the decision was made under (examples added from code included), and each finding from an example names it (`flag#3`, `acme:allow#1`), never its text.

## Limits

- Meaning matching uses static embeddings: they know words, not syntax, so "you are not an idiot" sits close to "you are an idiot". That is why only a close match flags and a looser one goes to the deep check. Add allow examples for the near misses you see.
- Examples are matched against the checked text only, not against earlier turns of a conversation.
- Up to 5,000 examples per list, each at most 4,000 characters.

---

# Deep check

> The optional tier 2 judge for what rules and local models are unsure about: on this machine or through an API

Source: https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/deep-check  |  Section: Python SDK

Rules and the local models settle most messages in milliseconds. When a score lands in a category's uncertain band, or a category has no local detector at that checkpoint, the guard can ask a slower, stronger model: the deep check.

Without one, uncertain findings are decided by the local score, and categories with no detector are recorded as `not_evaluated` (never as clean). `avaliar stats` shows how often that happened.

```yaml
judge:
  provider: local        # local, jev, anthropic, openai, gemini, groq, openrouter, avaliar, none
  timeout_ms: 60000      # how long the deep check may take
  within_budget: false   # true: fit inside the checkpoint's budget_ms instead
```

One deep-check call covers every unsettled category of a message, and only messages the local tiers could not settle are sent. The deep check gets its own wait (`timeout_ms`) on top of the checkpoint's `budget_ms`; `within_budget: true` keeps it inside the budget instead.

## The options

| `provider` | What runs | Needs | Leaves your machine |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local` | Clef-Flash 9B (a decision model) in a pinned `llama-server` on 127.0.0.1 | `avaliar judge install`, then `avaliar judge start`; about 7 GB of memory | Nothing |
| `jev` | TypeSafe's hosted decision model | `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` | The text being judged, to TypeSafe |
| `anthropic` | `claude-haiku-5-5` by default | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | The text, to Anthropic |
| `openai` | `gpt-4o-mini` by default; `base_url` reaches any OpenAI-compatible server, a local one included | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | The text, to that server |
| `gemini` | `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` by default | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | The text, to Google |
| `groq` | `openai/gpt-oss-120b` by default | `GROQ_API_KEY` | The text, to Groq |
| `openrouter` | `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` by default | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | The text, to OpenRouter |
| `avaliar` | Avaliar's tuned deep check (Pro plan) | `AVALIAR_API_KEY` | The text, to Avaliar Cloud |

`model`, `api_key_env` and `base_url` override the defaults. The first deep check logs one line saying which deep check is on and where text goes. See [What leaves your machine](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/network) for every request the SDK can make.

`local` and `jev` are decision models: they take the checked text as data and a yes/no question per category, and return a calibrated probability for each, with nothing to parse. The LLM APIs get a prompt and return JSON.

## The local deep check

```bash
avaliar judge install            # a pinned llama.cpp server (sha256 checked) and Clef-Flash (5.4 GB)
avaliar judge install --server-only
avaliar judge start              # 127.0.0.1:8080, in the background (--port, --threads)
avaliar judge status             # what is installed and whether it answers
avaliar judge stop
```

`avaliar doctor --measure` tells you whether this machine can run it, and how long a check takes. Expect 15 to 45 seconds per deep check on a laptop CPU, much less on a GPU.

> **Warning:** Clef-Flash's published scores are for fact checking, and its false block rate on agent safety tasks is high. Measure it on your own traffic before relying on it to block.

## Choosing

- **Nothing may leave the machine:** `local`.
- **Fast, and a hosted model is fine:** one of the LLM APIs. A deep check takes about a second and costs a fraction of a cent per unsettled message.
- **One place for your team's evidence too:** `avaliar`, with [Avaliar Cloud](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/cloud).

`avaliar init --how both --provider anthropic` writes a policy where local models check every message and the API sees only the unsure few. `avaliar doctor --online` sends one fixed test sentence to an API deep check to confirm the key works.

## When the deep check fails

A timeout, an error or an unreadable answer never counts as clean: the categories it was asked about keep their local score, or are recorded as `not_evaluated` with reason `judge_unavailable` (or `budget` when there was no time left). After `breaker_failures` failures in a row the guard stops calling it for `breaker_cooldown_s` seconds, so an outage does not slow every check.

---

# Evidence and verify

> The hash-chained local log of every decision, what it records, and how to check it was not changed

Source: https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/evidence  |  Section: Python SDK

With a policy file, every decision is appended to `.avaliar/evidence/*.jsonl`: one record per decision, linked into a hash chain. `avaliar verify` detects edits, deletions and reordering. The format is open JSON Lines, so any tool can read it.

```bash
avaliar logs                      # the last 50 records, newest last
avaliar logs -f --action block    # follow, only blocks
avaliar stats --since 7d          # counts by action, category and tier
avaliar verify                    # check every chain
```

## What a record holds

| Field | Contents |
|---|---|
| `id`, `ts`, `type` | A sortable id, the time, and `decision`, `approval`, `follow_up` or `gap` |
| `chain`, `seq`, `prev`, `hash` | The chain this record belongs to, its position, the previous record's hash and its own |
| `trace_id` | The trace the check belongs to |
| `checkpoint`, `name` | Where the check ran, and the tool or action name |
| `app`, `context` | The app name, and `session_id`, `agent`, `tenant`, `tags`, with `user_id` stored only as `user_id_hash` |
| `policy` | The policy's hash and path, and the hash of your example set |
| `input` | A keyed fingerprint of the checked text, its length, and the text at your capture level |
| `findings` | Category, detector name and version, tier, score and band for each finding |
| `not_evaluated` | Categories nothing could score, with the reason |
| `action`, `reasons` | The decision and why |
| `judge` | The deep check's provider, model, token usage and any error, when one ran |
| `latency_ms`, `sdk` | How long the check took and the SDK version |

Approvals are their own records, linked to the decision by `decision_id`, with who answered, when and how.

## How much text is kept

`evidence.capture` in the policy:

| Value | What is stored |
|---|---|
| `none` | No text at all, only the fingerprint and length |
| `redacted` (default) | The text with every piece of personal data or secret a detector found replaced, even where a rule only warned. Blocked text is not stored. |
| `full` | The text as checked |

User ids and inputs are fingerprinted with a per-install secret (`.avaliar/secret`, git-ignored by `avaliar init`), so the same input can be matched across records without storing it.

> **Warning:** `redacted` replaces what the detectors find. Anything they miss stays as written. Use `none` when no text may be kept.

## Chains and verification

Each writer process starts its own chain. Every record carries the previous record's hash, starting from a genesis value for the chain. Files rotate at `rotate_mb` (100 MB by default) and stay in the same chain.

`avaliar verify` recomputes every hash and link and reports, per chain:

| Problem | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `tampered` | A record's content does not match its hash |
| `broken_link` | A record's `prev` does not match the record before it |
| `seq_gap` | Records are missing from the middle of a chain |
| `out_of_order` | Records were reordered |
| `unparseable` | A line is not valid JSON |
| `truncated` | The last line was cut off (a crash mid-write); reported but not a failure |

It exits 0 when every chain verifies and 1 otherwise, so it fits in CI. `--json` gives a machine-readable report.

## Writes never break your app

Writes happen on a background thread with a bounded queue, so a check never waits on disk. A full queue drops records, counts them, and writes a `gap` record when it drains: gaps are visible, never silent. A read-only disk logs a warning and the checks carry on.

To make evidence a hard requirement, set `evidence.required: true`: writes become synchronous, a failed write is recorded on the decision as `not_evaluated` (`evidence_write_failed`), and with `on_error: fail_closed` the check blocks. The `strict` preset does this.

`d.evidence_ok` tells you whether a decision's record was written. Call `guard.flush()` before a short-lived process exits.

## Sending evidence to Avaliar Cloud

Set `AVALIAR_API_KEY` and the same records are uploaded from the local files in the background, re-verified on arrival, and shown on your team's dashboard. The local file stays the source of truth. See [Connecting to Avaliar Cloud](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/cloud).

---

# Error handling

> Checks never raise. What can, when, and how faults inside the guard are handled

Source: https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/error-handling  |  Section: Python SDK

The guard is built never to break your app. A check returns a `Decision`; it does not raise for a block, for a model that failed, for a deep check that timed out, or for evidence that could not be written.

Only three errors are ever raised, and two of them only when you ask:

| Error | When | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| `AvaliarPolicyError` | The policy is invalid, at `Guard(...)` construction (or `guard.add_examples` with an unknown category). Never per check. | `source`, `line`, `field` |
| `GuardBlocked` | A check blocks and you asked for an exception: `d.raise_for_block()`, `Guard(raise_on_block=True)`, or `@guard.tool` (by default) | `decision` |
| `GuardUnavailable` | A check could not complete, the checkpoint is `on_error: fail_closed`, and `raise_on_block=True` | `decision` |

All three subclass `AvaliarError`. `AvaliarPolicyError` is also a `ValueError`.

```python
from avaliar import AvaliarPolicyError, Guard, GuardBlocked

try:
    guard = Guard()
except AvaliarPolicyError as e:
    print(e.source, e.line, e.field, e)     # avaliar.yaml 12 input.rules.prompt injection.action ...
    raise

d = guard.check_input(message)
if d.blocked:
    return d.reply

try:
    guard.check_tool_call("send_email", args).raise_for_block()
except GuardBlocked as e:
    log.info("blocked: %s", e.decision.reasons)
```

`raise_for_block()` raises for `block` and for `approve` (a decision still waiting for a person), and returns the decision otherwise, so it chains.

## Faults inside the guard

A detector, a model or the deep check that fails is caught inside the guard and recorded. The categories it was meant to score are listed in `d.not_evaluated` with a reason (`error`, `judge_unavailable`, `budget` and others), and never counted as clean. What happens next is the checkpoint's `on_error` in the policy:

| `on_error` | Effect |
|---|---|
| `fail_open` (default) | The decision is made from what could be scored; the gap is recorded |
| `fail_closed` | The check blocks when a category whose rule would block or ask for approval could not be evaluated |

```yaml
input:
  on_error: fail_closed
```

Rules that fire still decide as usual. If the guard cannot even apply its rules or write back a redaction, it blocks rather than hand back text a rule wanted changed.

## Budgets

Each checkpoint has a time budget (`budget_ms`). Categories that could not finish in time are `not_evaluated` with reason `budget`, and `on_error` applies. The deep check gets `judge.timeout_ms` on top unless `judge.within_budget: true`. After repeated deep check failures a circuit breaker stops calling it for a while, so an outage does not slow every check.

## Evidence

Evidence is written off the request path. A failed write logs a warning and sets `d.evidence_ok = False`; it never raises. With `evidence.required: true` the write is synchronous, a failure is recorded as `not_evaluated` (`evidence_write_failed`), and with `on_error: fail_closed` the check blocks.

## Avaliar Cloud

The cloud link never breaks checking. Uploads run on a background thread; an outage, a timeout or a refused batch leaves the records on disk to upload later, and is logged. See [Connecting to Avaliar Cloud](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/cloud).

## Logging

Problems that need you are logged once to the `avaliar` logger at warning level: an invalid policy key with a warning, evidence that cannot be written, an unreachable deep check, a refused upload.

---

# Input

> Check what the user sends before it reaches your model

Source: https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/checkpoints/input  |  Section: SDK checkpoints

## When to call it

Before the message reaches your model. Pass the text, or the whole chat as a list of `{"role", "content"}` messages. With a chat, the last user message is checked by default; `scan` on the checkpoint changes which messages are read (see [Policy file](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/policy#checkpoints)).

```python
d = guard.check_input(user_message)
if d.blocked:
    return d.reply            # the policy's block reply
prompt = d.text               # redacted when a rule redacts
```

Send `d.text`, not the original, so redactions take effect. Uncertain categories that only warn may be checked after the reply (`speed.warn_after_reply`); their records follow the decision in the evidence log.

Default time budget: 300 ms (`input.budget_ms`). A deep check, when configured, may take `judge.timeout_ms` on top unless `judge.within_budget: true`.

## The recommended preset here

| Rule | Action | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| prompt injection | block | 0.8 |
| hidden text | block | 0.8 |
| sensitive data | redact | category default |

## Categories that can run here

| Category | Default threshold | Deep check | Needs | What it catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| blocklist | 0.5 | no | base install | Your own banned terms and patterns |
| custom | 0.7 | yes | a deep check | Your own criteria in plain English (`custom.<name>` with `criteria`) |
| gibberish | 0.7 | yes | a deep check for word salad | Keyboard mash, junk, token floods, word salad |
| harmful content | 0.7 | yes | a deep check | Bias, misinformation, misuse, graphic, illegal, personal safety, and personalised medical, legal or financial advice |
| hidden text | 0.5 | no | base install | Invisible or disguised characters: Unicode tags, bidi controls, zero-width runs, lookalike letters |
| language | 0.5 | no | base install | Not in the languages you allow |
| off topic | 0.85 | yes | a local model or a deep check | Outside the topics you allow |
| prompt injection | 0.8 | yes | `[local]` for the models | Attempts to take over or talk the model out of its rules: injected instructions, jailbreaks, poisoned tool descriptions |
| sensitive data | 0.5 | yes | base install | Personal data and secrets (keys, tokens, passwords); parts `personal` and `secrets` |
| toxicity | 0.8 | yes | `[local]` for the model | Abuse, harassment, threats |

See [Detectors and categories](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/detection) for the detectors behind each category and [Policy file](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/policy) for every rule option.

---

# Output

> Check what the model answers before the user sees it

Source: https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/checkpoints/output  |  Section: SDK checkpoints

## When to call it

After the model replies and before the user sees it. Pass the reply text, or the chat (the last assistant message is checked by default). Hallucination needs the documents the answer should rest on, as `context={"retrieval_context": [...]}`.

```python
d = guard.check_output(reply, context={"retrieval_context": docs})
return d.reply if d.blocked else d.text
```

Show `d.text`: secrets and personal data are already replaced with placeholders such as `[EMAIL_1]` where a rule redacts.

To catch a copied system prompt, plant a marker with `avaliar.new_canary()` and list it under the `data leak` rule's `canaries`, or pass the prompt as `context={"system_prompt": ...}`.

Default time budget: 1500 ms (`output.budget_ms`). A deep check, when configured, may take `judge.timeout_ms` on top unless `judge.within_budget: true`.

## The recommended preset here

| Rule | Action | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| sensitive data | redact | category default |
| sensitive data.secrets | block | category default |
| toxicity | block | 0.85 |
| harmful content | warn | category default |
| data leak | block | 0.8 |
| hidden text | redact | 0.8 |

## Categories that can run here

| Category | Default threshold | Deep check | Needs | What it catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| blocklist | 0.5 | no | base install | Your own banned terms and patterns |
| copyright | 0.7 | yes | a deep check for prose | Reproduced protected text or licensed code |
| custom | 0.7 | yes | a deep check | Your own criteria in plain English (`custom.<name>` with `criteria`) |
| data leak | 0.7 | no | base install | Data leaving through links and images, and the system prompt or a canary showing up in a reply; parts `links` and `system_prompt` |
| gibberish | 0.7 | yes | a deep check for word salad | Keyboard mash, junk, token floods, word salad |
| hallucination | 0.7 | yes | `retrieval_context`; a local model or a deep check | Claims not supported by the retrieval context |
| harmful content | 0.7 | yes | a deep check | Bias, misinformation, misuse, graphic, illegal, personal safety, and personalised medical, legal or financial advice |
| hidden text | 0.5 | no | base install | Invisible or disguised characters: Unicode tags, bidi controls, zero-width runs, lookalike letters |
| language | 0.5 | no | base install | Not in the languages you allow |
| off topic | 0.85 | yes | a local model or a deep check | Outside the topics you allow |
| sensitive data | 0.5 | yes | base install | Personal data and secrets (keys, tokens, passwords); parts `personal` and `secrets` |
| toxicity | 0.8 | yes | `[local]` for the model | Abuse, harassment, threats |

See [Detectors and categories](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/detection) for the detectors behind each category and [Policy file](https://docs.avaliar.ai/sdk/policy) for every rule option.
